pages.title: Nada y mucho (Arriaga, Juan Crisóstomo de)
pages.reason: Historical commentary conflicts over whether this is strictly three violins (Grove reportedly lists a basso part); inspect the complete score and establish a qualifying human performance before acceptance.

pages.title: Graded Course of Ensemble Playing (Auer, Leopold)
pages.reason: Auer presents a six-book teaching course with 2-violin duets, 4-violin pieces and optional piano; the page is a varied method collection, and the cached available piano volume is incomplete/illegible.

pages.title: Quartet for 4 Violins (Bacewicz, Grażyna)
pages.reason: The source page gives four separate violin parts and B.60; GAIA documents all three movements performed and released by four named violinists in 2024.

pages.title: Andante et Bourrée, Op.28 (Bachmann, Alberto)
pages.reason: Three separate violin parts and a ca.1903 Hamelle edition are listed, but no exact-version human performance or release was established in this pass.

pages.title: Blues, Espagnola und Rumba philharmonica (Blacher, Boris)
pages.reason: Boosey identifies a 12-solo-cello, three-movement work, duration 12 minutes, premiere 1973; a CD listing identifies the exact piece and Berliner Philharmonic 12 Cellists recording.

pages.title: Easy Trios for 3 Violins, Op.34 (Bloch, József)
pages.reason: The seven-piece set has three violin parts and a 1905 score source, but no actual human performance of the exact set was established; “Easy” alone does not determine eligibility.

pages.title: Violin Quartet (Bohm, Carl)
pages.reason: Four violin parts and a 1901 Simrock source are present, but no exact human performance/released recording was established.

pages.title: 6 String Quartets, Op.18 (Bréval, Jean-Baptiste)
pages.reason: This is a six-quartet collection with variable instrumentation; No. 5 is separately listed for four cellos, so it merits individual-work investigation, but no exact performance floor was established.

pages.title: 3 Sonatas for 3 Cellos (Cinque, Ermenegildo de)
pages.reason: The page supplies a manuscript score for three cello sonatas, but no performance or recording of the exact work/set was established.

pages.title: 3 Pieces for 4 Violins, Op.178 (Dancla, Charles)
pages.reason: The page supplies four violin parts for the three-piece set, but the linked Carl Fischer “five pieces” volume also contains works by Mozart and Schumann; extent and performance of the exact Dancla set need confirmation.

pages.title: 6 Petits trios faciles et concertants, Op.99 (Dancla, Charles)
pages.reason: The source collection has six violin trios and includes piano in the listed book score; an alternate three-violin guitar MIDI is not human-performance evidence, so accompaniment/version details and a real performance need review.

pages.title: La Réunion, Op.203 (Dancla, Charles)
pages.reason: Only the individual “Recueillement” score/parts and an unrelated guitar MIDI appear in the excerpt; the full three-piece set and a human performance floor were not confirmed.

pages.title: Le carnaval de Venise, Op.119 (Dancla, Charles)
pages.reason: The source lists four violin parts; a 2026 TKC Violin Quartet concert programme explicitly schedules Dancla’s Op.119 for four violins, supporting a real performance of the exact scoring.

pages.title: Variations on 'Ah! vous dirai-je, maman!', Op.161 (Dancla, Charles)
pages.reason: IMSLP lists a complete score plus four violin parts and links a free recording credited to Members of the Queensland Symphony Orchestra; recording identity/completeness should still be checked independently.

pages.title: Canon for 3 Violins (David, Ferdinand)
pages.reason: The source is a holograph manuscript for three violins, but no human performance/released recording was established.

pages.title: Arch (Davidson, Robert)
pages.reason: The original is for viola solo, but IMSLP separately lists a composer-made three-violin arrangement; treat that exact alternate scoring as its own candidate, pending performance evidence.

pages.title: Spiral 1 (Davidson, Robert)
pages.reason: IMSLP documents a cello-and-delay version or three cellos and offers a complete score; no actual three-cello performance was established, so the player-count version remains held.

pages.title: Gradus ad Parnassum, Op.52 (Dont, Jakob)
pages.reason: This is an ensemble-playing teaching collection with multiple mixed instrumentations and book-level selections, not one fixed scoring; inspect individual works only if they have independent concert evidence.

pages.title: Violin Quartet, Op.42 (Dont, Jakob)
pages.reason: A full score and four separate violin parts are listed for Op.42, but no exact-version human performance or recording was found in this first pass.

pages.title: Violin Quartet, Op.45 (Dont, Jakob)
pages.reason: The page is a distinct Op.45 identity with a published 3-violin/viola selection; the original 4-violin version lacks performance evidence here, and the selection must not be confused with it.
